questions.q: Mechanically, what determines whether an Account record is a person account or a business account?
options: The Account's billing address field
The Account field IsPersonAccount -- true for a person account record type, false for a business account
Whether the Account has any related Opportunities
The Account's record owner
questions.explain: Per Salesforce's SOAP API documentation, record types are person account record types if the Account field IsPersonAccount is set to true; business account record types have it set to false.

questions.q: What happens automatically when a person account is created, per Salesforce's documentation?
options: Nothing else is created
A corresponding 'person contact' record is also created, and it's the only contact record that can be associated directly with that person account
Two separate Contact records are created
A junction object record is created
questions.explain: Salesforce's documentation states that creating a person account also creates a corresponding person contact, which is uniquely bound to it -- a person account can never have a second, independent Contact.

questions.q: How does field-level security work for a person account field, according to Salesforce's documentation?
options: It is set directly and independently on the person account field
It is set on the corresponding Contact field, and the person account field inherits that same setting -- the two can't have different security
Person account fields have no field-level security
Field-level security only applies to business accounts
questions.explain: The lesson states that to set field-level security on a person account field, you set it on the corresponding Contact field, and the person account field inherits the identical setting.

questions.q: How does this lesson describe converting an existing business Account to a person account?
options: As a routine, one-click toggle with no real consequences
As a real, documented operation that Salesforce Help itself frames as having 'no easy way... but it can be done,' implying a one-way architectural decision
As something that is technically impossible on the platform
As something that automatically reverses itself after 30 days
questions.explain: The lesson quotes Salesforce Help's own framing directly to emphasize that this is a consequence-heavy decision that should be planned around, not flipped casually to 'see how it feels.'

questions.q: A healthcare network has individual Patients with no company involved, and separately, corporate Accounts sponsoring employee health plans. Per this lesson's framework, what does this mixed scenario suggest?
options: Person accounts should never be used in this org under any circumstances
Only business accounts and Contacts should ever be used, with no exceptions
This is exactly the mixed B2B/B2C case person accounts were built to coexist with business accounts for, but it needs a deliberate design pass for how reporting and workflows distinguish the two
The two populations should always be merged into a single person account model
questions.explain: The lesson identifies mixed B2B/B2C scenarios as the exact case where business accounts and person accounts are meant to coexist in the same org, while warning that this still requires deliberate design rather than an assumption that it'll just work.
